item.content:encoded:
China's Baidu tests robotaxi on London streets Reuters | Updated: 23-10-2026 17:30 IST | Created: 23-10-2026 17:30 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US-based Lyft unit Freenow and Baidu's Apollo Go unveiled the Chinese company's RT6 autonomous vehicle in London on Thursday and said they hope to launch a driverless robotaxi service in the city in 2027. The two companies began testing vehicles in London with safety drivers in the summer and hope to have fully driverless vehicles in the city next year, aiming for a commercial launch in 2027. The partnership between San Francisco-based ride-hailing firm Lyft and China's Baidu in London comes as the US Senate is working to pass a permanent ban on Chinese cars in the United States, pushing more companies to focus on Europe. Competition between robotaxi developers in London is heating up. UK self-driving vehicle startup Wayve and Lyft rival Uber launched a robotaxi service in London in September, initially with a human safety driver behind the wheel. US robotaxi company Waymo, a unit of Google parent Alphabet , aims to launch a fully driverless ride-hailing service in London by the end of this year. LONDON STREETS OFFER CHALLENGING TEST Freenow UK general manager Danny O'Gorman said London was a particularly good testing ground, with lots of speed bumps, narrow streets and many roads limited to 20 miles per hour. "So the car is going through the phase of learning the rules of the road much like you would do if you're trying to pass your own driving test," O'Gorman told Reuters during a demonstration ride. O'Gorman said the company was working closely with Transport for London and expected regulatory guidelines in the coming week. He recognised new technology "can sometimes be scary" but most Londoners were excited about the prospect He said robotaxis were not trying to replace London's famous black cabs. The firm is talking about "tens of vehicles in the next year or two" as it tests the market. "In terms of the taxi in London, the iconic black cab, this is not a replacement for that service," he said. "Black cabs are a fundamental part of London."

item.title: "No safe haven for Hamas," says Israel PM Netanyahu after terror attack in West Bank injures 5 people
item.description: Netanyahu condemned the attack and vowed that Israeli forces would continue to pursue Hamas who he said had no safe haven.
item.content:encoded:
"No safe haven for Hamas," says Israel PM Netanyahu after terror attack in West Bank injures 5 people Netanyahu condemned the attack and vowed that Israeli forces would continue to pursue Hamas who he said had no safe haven.  ANI | Updated: 23-10-2026 13:38 IST | Created: 23-10-2026 13:38 IST

Israeli security forces at incident site in Hebron (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Jerusalem [Israel], October 23 (ANI):  5 people were injured, 2 of them critically during a shooting incident in Hebron in the South West Bank in Israel. Israeli police said 2 gunmen involved in the terror attack were shot dead  IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir told the Times of Israel that the soldiers who killed the two Palestinian gunmen in the southern West Bank had prevented a more severe attack. “This was a serious attack. The troops’ swift action prevented an even more serious attack and further harm to civilians and security forces,” he said. Zamir says that “a large quantity of ammunition was found in the vehicle in which the terrorists arrived at the scene of the attack, which was intended to be used to carry out a larger-scale attack.” According to the IDF, the gunmen were armed with an M16 rifle and a pistol, and they were shot dead by the deputy commander of the Home Front Command’s Ari Battalion and a company commander who rushed to the scene. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned the attack and vowed that Israeli forces would continue to pursue Hamas who he said had no safe haven. "I have just concluded a situation assessment with the Minister of Defence, the Chief of the General Staff, the Head of the Shin Bet, the Head of the National Security Council, and the Commander of Central Command. I commend our heroic fighters who acted with determination and prevented a major terrorist attack, and I wish a speedy recovery to our wounded. I have instructed the IDF and the security forces to immediately impose a closure on the city of Hebron and to prepare for a full lockdown across all of Judea and Samaria starting today. Our forces are operating with enhanced strength to thwart terrorism and are carrying out extensive waves of arrests. We will pursue Hamas terrorists and their dispatchers everywhere and at all times. You have no safe haven," Netanyahu said. National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir called for the dismantling of the Palestinian Authority after the incident. “We have to act before it’s too late. The Palestinian Authority must be dismantled and demilitarized, and its terror infrastructure wiped out completely,” Ben Gvir said in a statement. The attack comes five days ahead of Israel’s elections. Prime Minister Netanyahu meanwhile directed the cancellation of all political events planned for this morning on behalf of the Likud Party. (ANI)

item.title: Pakistan forces face allegations of abuse, cash seizure during Nushki operation
item.description: Residents of Nushki district in Balochistan have accused Pakistan’s Frontier Corps (FC) personnel of mistreating civilians during a security operation and withholding cash seized during their ...
item.content:encoded:
Pakistan forces face allegations of abuse, cash seizure during Nushki operation Residents of Nushki district in Balochistan have accused Pakistan’s Frontier Corps (FC) personnel of mistreating civilians during a security operation and withholding cash seized during their detention, as reported by The Balochistan Post. ANI | Updated: 23-10-2026 13:05 IST | Created: 23-10-2026 13:05 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Residents of Nushki district in Balochistan have accused Pakistan’s Frontier Corps (FC) personnel of mistreating civilians during a security operation and withholding cash seized during their detention, as reported by The Balochistan Post. According to The Balochistan Post, several residents of Killi Faqiran were detained on suspicion following a shooting on the bypass road near the Deputy Commissioner’s residence two days earlier. The individuals were subsequently released after questioning. In a written complaint submitted to the Inspector General of FC Balochistan and the Corps Commander, the affected residents alleged that security personnel entered their homes, verbally abused them and instructed all men to assemble at a designated location. The complainants claimed that personnel confiscated their mobile phones, wallets and cash. They said they counted the money they were carrying before handing it over to the security personnel. The residents further alleged that their shirt hems were tied together before they were taken to FC headquarters and compelled to raise slogans during the journey. Although their phones and wallets were reportedly returned after their release, the cash allegedly remained missing. When they sought the return of their money, personnel allegedly dismissed their concerns. The complainants have urged the Corps Commander, the FC Inspector General and other senior officials to conduct an impartial investigation into the alleged mistreatment, damage to their homes and disappearance of their money. They have also demanded legal proceedings and departmental action against those found responsible. The residents stated that alleged high-handedness against ordinary citizens could further aggravate public resentment in Nushki, where security concerns and tensions remain significant, as highlighted by The Balochistan Post. The allegations come amid similar complaints from other parts of Balochistan. In September, residents of Kasano in Tump, Kech district, accused Pakistani forces of conducting house searches, taking valuables, physically abusing residents and setting fire to a house belonging to Ikram Baloch, as reported by The Balochistan Post. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Indian Embassy and Consulate in Saudi Arabia extending full support to affected pilgrims: MEA India is assisting stranded Umrah pilgrims in Saudi Arabia, with around 3,000 returning home over the past week. The government is coordinating with airlines and tour operators. This follows an airport attack in Dammam that killed two people, including an Indian national, and injured others. ANI | Updated: 22-10-2026 17:33 IST | Created: 22-10-2026 17:33 IST

Surveillance footage shows people standing, right before the moment of an attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

India's diplomatic missions in Saudi Arabia are actively engaging with concerned airlines and tour operators to facilitate the early return of affected pilgrims, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) announced on Thursday. Tragedy struck on Wednesday when an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Saudi Arabia's Dammam resulted in the death of an Indian national among two fatalities, alongside two other Indian nationals sustaining injuries. According to official figures released by the MEA, approximately 3,000 stranded Umrah pilgrims have travelled back to India over the past week, utilising available flights. "This is in addition to more than 10,000 normal Umrah pilgrims who were booked on the available flights and have travelled back to India over the past week," the ministry stated. "Arrangements are being discussed to facilitate the return of other Umrah pilgrims at the earliest. Our Embassy and Consulate, with the support from community volunteers, are extending all possible welfare assistance. 24×7 Control Rooms have been established to help Indian nationals and regular advisories are being issued." Earlier in the day, the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia confirmed that it was gathering further details and reaching out to the families affected following the Dammam airport attack. "Saudi authorities have informed that one Indian national was among two people who unfortunately lost their lives in the attack on Dammam airport yesterday night and two Indian nationals were injured. We are ascertaining further details and contacting the affected families. Our thoughts and prayers are with the family and loved ones of the deceased and we wish speedy recovery of the injured," the embassy noted in a post on X. Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) reported that Wednesday's attack targeting the facility claimed two lives, comprising one Indian resident and one Saudi citizen, while leaving eight individuals injured. Providing a comprehensive breakdown via X, the Saudi civil aviation authority clarified, "Further to its earlier statement regarding the attack that targeted King Fahd International Airport in Dammam on the evening of Wednesday, October 21, 2026, corresponding to 10 Jumada Al-Awwal 1448 AH, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) clarifies that the number of fatalities has risen to (2) after an additional fatality was confirmed, involving (1) Saudi citizen and (1) Indian resident. The number of the injured remains at (8), including (1) Saudi citizen, and residents of the following nationalities: (2) Indian, (2) Yemeni, (2) Bangladeshi and (1) Nepalese. Their injuries range from minor to critical, and they are receiving the necessary medical care at several hospitals." The Saudi civil aviation authority added that it is coordinating closely with relevant departments to evaluate structural damage, verify facility safety, protect personnel and passengers, and uphold the security of the national aviation network. Operations at the airport have since resumed, alongside the restoration of normal air traffic flows. Meanwhile, New Delhi issued a strong condemnation of ongoing attacks directed at civilian and energy infrastructure within Saudi Arabia, encompassing the Dammam airport strike and an incident at Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oil field, while voicing hope for a swift return to peace and normalcy across the region. "We strongly condemn the continued attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including the attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oil field in the Eastern Province on October 21. These attacks have unfortunately resulted in civilian deaths and injuries," the MEA stated. Reaffirming New Delhi's firm stance, the ministry added, "We also reiterate that the attacks on civilian and critical infrastructure are completely unacceptable and must cease immediately. We stand in solidarity with the people and the Government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its sovereignty, and hope that peace and normalcy would return to the region at the earliest." (ANI)
